entries.subject: Placement
entries.finding: Gaia DR3 source 1939115478598580352: position at J2016.0. Distance: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 116584: distance 26.406 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.006), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 26.406 +/- 0.158 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 38.5736 +/- 0.1179 mas (same row, RUWE 2.47), 327.1 standard errors, is not used. Proper motion: Gaia DR3 (same row): 159.606, -421.822 mas/yr. Radial velocity from SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 1939115478598580352 (quality A), from 2004MNRAS.349.1069K; Gaia DR3 measures none.

entries.subject: Radius, mass and temperature
entries.finding: Radius 7.552 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 116584: radius 7.552 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 24.306 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.054) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4667 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 116584: effective temperature 4667 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.037).

entries.subject: Limb darkening
entries.finding: The disc is dimmed toward the limb by the power law I(mu) = mu^0.231 that Martinez et al. (2021), ApJ 916, 60 fit to the star's resolved disc (CHARA/MIRC H band, 1.5-1.7 um; not a visible band).

entries.subject: mirc visibilities of 2 to 24 September 2011 as a surface map
entries.finding: The authors' calibrated files of 6 nights (2 September 2011: 360 squared visibilities; 6 September 2011: 392 squared visibilities; 10 September 2011: 360 squared visibilities; 14 September 2011: 864 squared visibilities; 19 September 2011: 808 squared visibilities; 24 September 2011: 200 squared visibilities) are public with their code. ROTIR at the pinned commit (HEALPix level 3, sobel2 at weight 10, 1000 iterations) fits one turning surface to all of them. The fit leaves a reduced chi-squared of 1.72 on the squared visibilities and 2.30 on the closure phases, where a spotless star leaves 3.13 and 28.29 (limit 3); its spots are 2.14 times those the same fit draws on a spotless star of 2.77 mas (limit 2); and two independent halves of the data give the same spots (correlation 0.83, limit 0.5). Spotless twins of 2.69 mas and 2.80 mas do not fit on the 2.742 mas sphere (closure-phase chi-squared 7.42 and 9.40) and so do not decide the spot check. The published maps themselves are not redistributed.

entries.subject: Rotation axis, period and prime meridian
entries.finding: The page draws the axis the surface map is fitted with: inclination 85.63° and pole position angle 26.09° east of north, with a period of 54.2 d (Martinez et al. (2021), ApJ 916, 60, Table 4 (https). No prime meridian is defined for the star: longitude 0 is the meridian that faced the Earth on 14 September 2011, and the star is not turned.
